# Approved data A/B implementation design

Root released this stage after the source-bound mechanical gate. Exact authority: `t2-t3-po-architecture-revalidation.json` items A/B and applied receipt. No lifecycle/QA verdict.

Guided unreached identity uses the exact immutable manifest referenceId/declaring step and current terminal fence. Actual ordinal/admission/resolution/release/version/sequence are absent. Stable declaration duplication and any retained real consume/decision/summary exclude false unused across fences/time. Consumed unknown keeps real admission/ordinal/proposal/materialization source-reference provenance/fence, with no fictitious release sequence.

B agrees `recordObservedReadEntry(binding, actualLeaseOwner, secretId)` in a committed caller transaction before each existing value read; no additional provider call. `recordObservedNoSend(binding, actualLeaseOwner, positivelyNotEnteredIds, CLOSED|REQUEUED)` appends a safe receipt and unlinked NOT_USED rows before the winning owner transition in the same locked transaction. IDs originate positively from the accepted declaration iterator minus entered reads and actual decisions, never missing FINAL/decision rows. Receipt insertion validates live owned CLAIMED/no current attempt/admission/receipt and the accepted binding/revision/scope. A per-leaf deferred constraint verifies the final logical CLOSED (actual ledger DONE/history ERROR) or outage QUEUED state and exact accepted identity. CLOSED preserves the existing recorded owner or a cleared lease; QUEUED requires the existing cleared lease, plus actual ledger row version written by this transaction and exactly one summary for each positive ID. Receipt-only commit, rollback, stale/losing closure and post-send inference refuse. No new retry authority.

Both safe evidence families use occurred_at partitions under existing 12-month retention, no DEFAULT, owner-row→owner-advisory→event lock order, immutable row and direct-leaf TRUNCATE guards. Actual read-entry/receipt linkage is scoped and verified at insert; no self-FK prevents bounded partition retention. Actual caller/Vault counters and joined kill/crash/send oracles remain B/T4 obligations.

PostgreSQL15 documents that each update creates a row version whose xmin is the inserting transaction identity; xid8 can be cast to xid. The deferred comparison is local to the current transaction, not a long-term transaction-ID identity. Current B caller uses one physical joined transaction without savepoint-based state transitions. Deferred constraints are installed on plain leaf partitions; future partition manager installs identical guards.

Primary sources: [system columns](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/15/ddl-system-columns.html), [transaction functions](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/15/functions-info.html), [constraint triggers](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/15/sql-createtrigger.html).

An ordinary replay read-entry followed by controller crash before a committed resolution has no approved unlinked UNKNOWN shape. This stage refuses false NOT_USED and retains the unmatched summary obligation explicitly for a narrow independent Aria/PO proposal; SQL metadata is not physical-read proof.

Any ID with an actual decision remains linked. No crash or missing decisionFacts can manufacture the set. Guard from locked authentic CLAIMED/current lease with no dispatch attempt/admission/observed receipt/sendCommitted; receipt, audit and winning close/outage-requeue commit together or all roll back. A guarded database transition constraint or equivalent database-verified owner interface prevents receipt-only commit; caller flags are insufficient. Keep owner row→owner advisory→event lock order, cross-month deduplication and Q3 receipt/audit retention alignment. The receipt provides no refreshRetry, deadline, grant or CAS authority: zero_send_decision_attempt_id remains limited to real VAULT_UNAVAILABLE outage CLAIMED→QUEUED provenance, definite_refusal_attempt_id to authentic transport refusal. Post-send/no-admission ambiguity is excluded. Supporting receipts are the existing RunnerReport.steps[] objects, exactly {stepIndex,status,startedAtMs,finishedAtMs,durationMs,failure}; they gain no stepId, sourceInputId, secretId, admission or other wire field. Validate raw receipts before projection/rounding; missing, duplicate, regressing, failed, started-only, skipped or contradictory receipts cannot establish new USED. # Synkra AIOX Constitution

> **Version:** 1.1.0 | **Ratified:** 2025-01-30 | **Last Amended:** 2026-07-09  
> **Amendments:** Articles XI–XII (CORE-SUPER-UPDATE Wave E; hub lineage, OSS-safe)

Este documento define os princípios fundamentais e inegociáveis do Synkra AIOX. Todos os agentes, tasks, e workflows DEVEM respeitar estes princípios. Violações são bloqueadas automaticamente via gates.

---

## Core Principles

### I. CLI First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

O CLI é a fonte da verdade onde toda inteligência, execução, e automação vivem.

**Regras:**
- MUST: Toda funcionalidade nova DEVE funcionar 100% via CLI antes de qualquer UI
- MUST: Dashboards apenas observam, NUNCA controlam ou tomam decisões
- MUST: A UI NUNCA é requisito para operação do sistema
- MUST: Ao decidir onde implementar, sempre CLI > Observability > UI

**Hierarquia:**
```
CLI (Máxima) → Observability (Secundária) → UI (Terciária)
```

**Gate:** `dev-develop-story.md` - WARN se UI criada antes de CLI funcional

---

### II. Agent Authority (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

Cada agente tem autoridades exclusivas que não podem ser violadas.

**Regras:**
- MUST: Apenas @devops pode executar `git push` para remote
- MUST: Apenas @devops pode criar Pull Requests
- MUST: Apenas @devops pode criar releases e tags
- MUST: Agentes DEVEM delegar para o agente apropriado quando fora de seu escopo
- MUST: Nenhum agente pode assumir autoridade de outro

**Exclusividades:**

| Autoridade | Agente Exclusivo |
|------------|------------------|
| git push | @devops |
| PR creation | @devops |
| Release/Tag | @devops |
| Story creation | @sm, @po |
| Architecture decisions | @architect |
| Quality verdicts | @qa |

**Gate:** Implementado via definição de agentes (não requer gate adicional)

---

### III. Story-Driven Development (MUST)

Todo desenvolvimento começa e termina com uma story.

**Regras:**
- MUST: Nenhum código é escrito sem uma story associada
- MUST: Stories DEVEM ter acceptance criteria claros antes de implementação
- MUST: Progresso DEVE ser rastreado via checkboxes na story
- MUST: File List DEVE ser mantida atualizada na story
- SHOULD: Stories seguem o workflow: @po/@sm cria → @dev implementa → @qa valida → @devops push

**Gate:** `dev-develop-story.md` - BLOCK se não houver story válida

---

### IV. No Invention (MUST)

Especificações não inventam - apenas derivam dos requisitos.

**Regras:**
- MUST: Todo statement em spec.md DEVE rastrear para:
  - Um requisito funcional (FR-*)
  - Um requisito não-funcional (NFR-*)
  - Uma constraint (CON-*)
  - Um finding de research (verificado e documentado)
- MUST NOT: Adicionar features não presentes nos requisitos
- MUST NOT: Assumir detalhes de implementação não pesquisados
- MUST NOT: Especificar tecnologias não validadas

**Gate:** `spec-write-spec.md` - BLOCK se spec contiver invenções

---

### V. Quality First (MUST)

Qualidade não é negociável. Todo código passa por múltiplos gates antes de merge.

**Regras:**
- MUST: `npm run lint` passa sem erros
- MUST: `npm run typecheck` passa sem erros
- MUST: `npm test` passa sem falhas
- MUST: `npm run build` completa com sucesso
- MUST: CodeRabbit não reporta issues CRITICAL
- MUST: Story status é "Done" ou "Ready for Review"

### 5.5 SSE progress

`GET /executions/{id}/events` returns `text/event-stream` using Spring MVC `SseEmitter`. Initial and reconnect delivery is a full current execution snapshot. Event type is `execution.snapshot`; `id` is the API snapshot revision. The MFE replaces current state, ignores older revisions, and never re-executes because a connection failed.

Each API replica batches DB reads for its locally watched execution IDs every 500–1000 ms and broadcasts only changed snapshots. Share a read across viewers of a run; no sticky sessions or broker are required. Intermediate transitions may coalesce, but final step status, timings, and bounded retained logs survive. `Last-Event-ID` supports reconnect identification; V1 promises current-state recovery, not lossless event replay. Include `logsTruncated` when the configured retained-log cap is reached.

Send heartbeat comments every 15 seconds. Use an explicit bounded stream lifetime (initially 60 seconds) and reconnect to refresh identity/CSI authorization. Set `Cache-Control: no-store`; disable buffering through the actual gateway/ingress; idle timeouts must exceed heartbeat cadence. Native EventSource uses the approved session-cookie route; a bearer-only platform requires a header-capable client inside the centralized API service. No credential query parameters. Verify cross-origin cookie/CORS behavior where applicable.

Use bounded dedicated senders and coalesced per-client pending snapshots; slow clients must not block callbacks, DB readers, or ordinary check workers. Clean up on error/timeout/completion and component unmount. One subscription per actively viewed execution. Close explicitly on `streamComplete=true`, after evidence is settled. On persistent transport failure use the authorized GET snapshot with bounded polling; distinguish 401/403 via the normal client and stop rather than falling back around denied access.

Validate streaming through the actual proxy/auth route before rollout; a demonstrated incompatibility uses GET fallback without changing the execution contract. [Spring MVC](https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/web/webmvc/mvc-ann-async.html) supports this streaming model.

## 6. Video proof & playback

### 6.1 Recording and evidence state

Record native webm on the single page's context. Await context closure to finalize the file; sudden process death may leave no playable recording. Explicitly configure video resolution so the text needed for evidence remains readable. [Playwright video documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/videos) describes context finalization and per-page recordings.

Keep outcome (`PASSED | FAILED | ERROR`) separate from evidence: `PROCESSING | AVAILABLE | FAILED | UNAVAILABLE | EXPIRED`. Upload failure never overwrites a known assertion outcome. `UNAVAILABLE` covers runs without a usable recording; `FAILED` covers evidence production/upload failures. Expose `videoError`, `videoExpiresAt`, and whether an available recording is partial. `streamComplete` means run processing/evidence delivery is settled, not that retention can no longer change availability.

### 6.2 Storage

Private keys:

- Video: `studio/{csiId}/{testId}/{executionId}/{attemptId}.webm`.
- Result manifest: `studio/{csiId}/{testId}/{executionId}/{attemptId}.result.json`.

The API derives expected keys from immutable execution identity; client-supplied keys are never trusted. Runner writes only this prefix; API/recovery read only. Runner has no Get/List permissions. Use encrypted transport/storage under platform policy. Manifests and videos expire after 30 days via lifecycle rules; verify versioning/noncurrent-object and incomplete-upload cleanup semantics on Sonic. Enforce logical video expiry in the API at `videoExpiresAt` even if physical lifecycle deletion is asynchronous. Track deletion compliance; do not claim exact-time physical deletion before Sonic behavior is verified.

### 6.3 Playback and download

`GET /executions/{id}/video` checks the execution's immutable CSI, including for soft-deleted tests, then streams from Sonic. Support ordinary 200, single byte Range/206, valid `Content-Range`, and invalid/unsatisfiable range 416. Return a clear expired/unavailable response when appropriate. `?download=true` uses the same authorization with an attachment filename derived by the API. Store object keys only; expose the protected API path to the browser.
